scope_note: Directed fourth-pass project-scoped evidence audit of Google's Douglas County data-center campus at 300 Riverside Parkway SW. The selected IM3 object is a campus, and the public record resolves a Development Authority real-property parcel, two Google-linked personal-property accounts, two assessor-classified data-center buildings, a utility building, later permit work, utility-customer history, a permitted discharge facility, and off-site supporting solar infrastructure; no record is allocated below its published scope. Twenty-six observations are added: twenty-four reported actuals and two source projections. County taxpayer totals and account-level assessed values overlap and must not be summed; exempt assessed value is not taxable value or tax avoided, appraised real-property value is not investment, permit value is not spending, contracted solar capacity is not facility load, and community amounts have distinct recipients and periods. Direct tax payments, executed incentive schedules, utility bills, observed establishment payroll, worker residence, local supplier payments, same-scope public-service costs, and causal county outcomes remain unresolved rather than zero.

project_updates.title: Campus identity and chronology resolved
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: IM3 inventory, Google location and sustainability pages, Douglas County assessor records, Georgia EPD permits, and contemporaneous expansion reporting. The project boundary is the Google-operated campus at 300 Riverside Parkway on authority-owned parcel 08741820001. Google dates its Douglas County presence to 2003 and first data-center opening to 2007; the assessor dates Computer Data Centers improvements to 2006 and 2016 and a utility building to 2011. Later Google Georgia projects in LaGrange and Columbia County, an account at 2201 Thornton Road, unrelated Douglas County DRI data-center proposals, and off-site solar projects are not collapsed into the campus.
project_updates.project_description: Google operates the Douglas County data-center campus at 300 Riverside Parkway SW in Lithia Springs on a Development Authority of Douglas County tax-abatement parcel. Google dates its local presence to 2003 and its first data-center opening to 2007; the assessor lists data-center improvements with actual years 2006 and 2016 and a utility building from 2011. Public records also document a 2015 expansion, recycled-water cooling, later interior-remodel work, and off-site solar procurement supporting the campus.

project_updates.title: Assessor and taxpayer-account audit separates taxable and exempt stocks
project_updates.notes: Repositories and routes checked: Douglas qPublic real- and personal-property searches, linked-account tables, Board of Tax Assessors agendas, 2019-2024 County ACFR principal-taxpayer and millage exhibits, Georgia DOR property-record and millage files, and exact Google/DADC/address/parcel/account queries. P88150 is the directly named Google account; P79020 is authority-owned with Google tax-department linkage and fully exempt assessed value. The 2026 account and parcel stocks are recorded separately. The March 5, 2025 BTA agenda's P79020 amended-return figures conflict with the retained live historical 2024 figure and are documented as interim or superseded, not recorded. P97430 at 2201 Thornton Road and contractor, food-service, Waymo, logistics, or empty linked accounts are excluded. County totals, real parcel value, and account components overlap and are not summed.

project_updates.title: Tax-bill and payment search remains blocked after account resolution
project_updates.notes: Repositories and routes checked: Tax Commissioner pages and reports, Georgia DOR payment routing and 2023-2025 millage files, GovernmentWindow tax.html and its select_bill.html GET workflow, qPublic histories, County ACFR tax collections/millage exhibits, document-center search, and indexed exact queries for P79020, P88150, 08741820001, Google, DADC, and 300 Riverside Parkway. The portal exposes tax years 2017-2026 and map/parcel/property-ID, bill-number, address, and owner modes, but Cloudflare Turnstile guards the search; the CAPTCHA was not solved or bypassed, and alternate indexed queries yielded no bill. Assessed or exempt value is not called tax avoided, billed, paid, collected, delinquent, or distributed. Two county-M&O gross-levy counterfactuals are modeled from published inputs, explicitly not payment or realized abatement.

Russell & Company; electrical permit 2502513-DC names Allison-Smith Company but displays zero value, treated as missing rather than zero cost. project_updates.title: County outcome and public-cost candidates fail causal and fiscal prerequisites
project_updates.notes: BLS QCEW, BEA county accounts, Census business and population context, County ACFRs and budgets, and development records were checked for employment, establishments, wages, income, GDP, population, property-tax share, capital spending, public safety, roads, water, and debt from 2001 through the latest complete vintages. Google dates local presence to 2003 and opening to 2007, while concurrent county growth, multiple later data centers, boundary changes, the 2008 recession, and missing treatment-share and comparison diagnostics prevent a defensible project effect. County totals remain context only. No same-scope marginal service cost, attributable infrastructure outlay, fiscal recipient distribution, or validated counterfactual was found.

project_updates.title: Fourth-pass model audit retains bounded anchor-based estimates and rejects unsupported chains
project_updates.notes: Candidate-by-candidate disposition after directed exhaustion: retain three unallocated 2022-2024 water-consumption conversions; annualize the displayed 2026 ECHO DMR average flow with a rounding band; calculate two county-M&O-only gross-levy counterfactuals from exempt P79020 assessed value and published millage; apply Douglas County's 2015 all-industry QCEW wage to the operator's 350-employee threshold with a 75%-125% wage sensitivity; and apply a national 2022 construction payroll/receipts ratio to the sole valued 2025 remodel with 0.5-1.5 transfer sensitivity. Reject supplier/local-purchase models for missing payments and geography; energy use/cost because solar and PUE are not load; actual abatement, net fiscal benefit, and public cost because bills, executed schedules, distributions, and same-scope costs are absent; and county outcomes for missing causal design. Wider Oxford/Deloitte effects remain context, not re-labeled observations.

project_updates.title: Directed fourth-pass source matrix records exact identifiers and unresolved gaps
project_updates.notes: Exact official identifiers and years checked across the matrix: parcel 08741820001 and accounts P88150/P79020 (2023-2026); BTA P79020 amended return (March 5, 2025); County M&O rates (2023-2024); GovernmentWindow tax years 2017-2026; DADC Google lease amendment (October 17, 2023) and DCA 2008 debt entries; WSA Google customer tables (2007, 2014, 2016), Data Center Water Demands agenda item (December 11, 2023), and rates effective December 1, 2024; NPDES GA0038920/FRS 110061650100 and ECHO 2026 DMR; EPD application 27010, order EPD-AQ-6038, complaint 75360; PSC Docket 55378; permits 2502392-DC/2502513-DC; 2015 operator and 2016 principal-employer counts; recipient confirmations and nonprofit filings. Remaining gaps are bills/payments, executed fiscal instruments, utility agreements/meters, historic permit attachments, invoices/vendor geography, observed Google payroll/residence/training transfers, and same-scope public costs—not zeros.
